title: ComfyUI is up with no claim on the 4090 while holding 20.6 GB
evidence: port 8188 answering, state=idle, the instance itself holds 21142MiB of the card's 23300MiB (threshold 8192MiB); the instance is IDLE -- native queue empty and last prompt 110 min ago (live window 30 min) -- so this VRAM is residue the next claimant renders against. owner=foreign pid=1625701 cgroup=/user.slice/user-1000.slice/user@1000.service/app.slice/hermes-webui.service started=Fri_Oct__9_22:22:08_2026 reserve=missing holder=agent. A foreign instance is not ours to kill (harness ownership rule): shut it down from its own session, or accept the hold.

notes.note: 2026-09-23 05:4xZ ops-triage: DECIDED -- accept the hold (yield), and made the check's claim TRUE BY CONSTRUCTION. Condition is real: pid 553489 (holder=operator, his byobu/tmux session, started Tue Sep 22 18:49 EDT) is IDLE (native queue empty, last prompt 62 min) holding 18,438 of the card's 18,945 MiB with no claim and no --reserve-vram. But the title asserted that from the CARD-level reading (nvidia-smi memory.used = an upper bound counting every co-tenant), so a labeler holding 14 GiB beside an idle ComfyUI holding 300 MiB produced the same reading AND the same title -- a false attribution that sends a reader to shut down the wrong process. FIX (bin/tc_ops.py): new pure unclaimed_vram_verdict(card_mib, own_mib) + comfyui_instance_vram_mib() (per-pid, --query-compute-apps): the instance's OWN hold decides; a co-tenant's VRAM makes the check quiet; an unreadable own-hold keeps the detection but is worded as the card's, never the instance's. Verified: selftest 451/0 (9 new branches: co-tenant-holds-it -> quiet, own-unreadable -> still fires); live re-run prints 'the instance itself holds 18438MiB of the card's 18945MiB' and still fires. DECISION: YIELD -- a foreign operator session is not ours to kill or re-flag; the render impact is render-starved's warn, and that refusal is over-determined (launch-args gate first, then free 5.0GiB < 16GiB floor). Escalation criterion unchanged (pre-registered by the overnight watchdog): dry_out inside ~3 days while refusals continue -- currently 09-29T10:30Z (6.3d), so no Tim ask.

NOT filed, and the card is still held: the :8188 instance (pid 553489) is the OPERATOR's own interactive session -- no agent may touch it, its launch line is not ours to change, and the harness ownership rule says yield. FIXED root cause: classifier mis-attribution. The open instance pid 1625701 (ComfyUI holding 20.6GB, native queue empty) is the OPERATOR's interactive WebUI session -- launched from hermes-webui/server.py, cgroup=hermes-webui.service, owner=foreign -- but classify_holder returned 'agent' because the cgroup contains 'hermes', so the check filed an agent decision for a session no agent may touch. Fixed classify_holder: hermes-webui.service now classifies 'operator' BEFORE the generic hermes->agent rule (harness's own instance lives in comfyui-svc-* and is unaffected -> 'unit'). VERIFIED:  now prints operator; synthetic classifier table passes (hermes-webui->operator, comfyui-svc->unit, hermes-worker->agent). The check now note_quiets this operator session (render starvation is already escalated on render-starved route=tim), so the item stops being filed.
